name: Mike Stapleton
caption: Half of a tag team absorbed from a rival federation's own closure, introduced on the destination's television alongside a tribute package recapping a plane crash, a car crash reported at the time as fatal, and an in-fiction recovery.

tenures.source: cited, not served under this wing (HWL's own tribute package, narrated by its merchandising announcer, promotions/necw/archive/necw-matchat-introducing-1997-11-22.html)

name: Mark Stapleton
caption: The other half of the absorbed Stapleton tag team; on-air, the promotion's own president says Mark was out eight months after a real-world-framed plane crash before returning that September.

tenures.source: cited, not served under this wing (HWL's own tribute package, narrated by its merchandising announcer, promotions/necw/archive/necw-matchat-introducing-1997-11-22.html)

name: Ted O'Shea
caption: Billed as "TOS," a former HWL titleholder signed to chase old HWL rivals in his new home, introduced with a rambling, nose-picking vignette rather than a straight promo.

tenures.source: cited, not served under this wing ("he held a stack of titles in HWL," promotions/necw/archive/necw-matchat-introducing-1997-11-22.html)

name: Whole Life
caption: A former HWL television and tag team champion (and, before that, a PWF wrestler) who arrives with a stack of rejected life-insurance-application cue cards for his old rivals.

tenures.source: cited, not served under this wing ("former HWL television and tag team champion," promotions/necw/archive/necw-matchat-introducing-1997-11-22.html)

name: "The Ultimate Cool Dude" Log
caption: The HWL's own reigning World Heavyweight Champion, billed by his manager and sister as a six-time HWL World Champion who also held North American, TV and two sets of tag team titles there.

tenures.source: cited, not served under this wing ("Six world titles in the HWL. A North American belt. A TV belt. Two world tag straps. Two TV tag belts. All in a year and a half," promotions/necw/archive/necw-matchat-introducing-1997-11-22.html)

name: Ravishing Rebecca
caption: Log's manager and older sister, who narrates his HWL title history to camera while showing off one of his old championship belts.

name: "SuperNova" Sammi Stoughton
caption: Named in the Stapletons' own HWL tribute package as a fellow crash survivor, and appears alongside them on their new federation's own arrival segment.

tenures.source: cited, not served under this wing (HWL's own tribute package, promotions/necw/archive/necw-matchat-introducing-1997-11-22.html)

name: Ben Grimes
caption: Billed as the Stapletons' longtime friend and Mark's tag partner during his HWL comeback, appearing alongside them on their new federation's own arrival segment.

tenures.source: cited, not served under this wing (HWL's own tribute package, promotions/necw/archive/necw-matchat-introducing-1997-11-22.html)

name: Jack Skar
notes: Known from one post to rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy (13 March 1998), served at /promotions/rspwf/archive/flash-being-posted-for-evaluation-1998-03-13.html: Jack Skar, standing in the Skar Wrestling School's gym in Bay City, Michigan, warns the Zookeeper that his abuse of Gorilla will cost him at the pay-per-view, and tells how his late son Erik's death still drives his son Jacob.
caption: The trainer, manager and father of Jacob Skar, who runs the Skar Wrestling School in Bay City, Michigan.

name: Jacob Skar
notes: Known from one post to rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy (13 March 1998), served at /promotions/rspwf/archive/flash-being-posted-for-evaluation-1998-03-13.html: Jack Skar, standing in the Skar Wrestling School's gym in Bay City, Michigan, warns the Zookeeper that his abuse of Gorilla will cost him at the pay-per-view, and tells how his late son Erik's death still drives his son Jacob.
caption: An NECW tag champion who has never recovered from the death of his brother Erik, March 1998.
